*Stock Exchange of Thailand Expects 'Double-Digit' IPOs in 2027, Top Exec Says
*Thailand's Secondary Market Activity Seeing Renewed Surge, Top Exec Says
*Investors Seem Optimistic About Thai Stocks Amid Low Valuations, Top Exec Says
Thai Stock Exchange Bets on Market Revival as Foreign Money Returns — Interview
By Amanda Lee
Thailand isn't typically the first market that comes to mind when thinking about investing in Asia. The country's stock-exchange operator says that's changing.
The Stock Exchange of Thailand is banking on a strengthening stock market and the return of foreign capital to stoke a revival in investing and listings activity.
Relatively low valuations have prompted investors to "come back and take a look" at Thailand, said Soravis Krairiksh, chief markets officer and senior executive vice president at the SET.
"They start to see that there is a compelling narrative, a story for them to be locked in for their investment in the longer term," he said.
Thailand's stock market has emerged as the best performer in Southeast Asia so far this year, with the benchmark SET Index up 28%. Last year, it shed 10%.
Still, initial public offerings have been lackluster. Only three companies have listed so far this year, with just one on the SET's main board.
"I've written off this year," Soravis said.
But he still projects that the number of debuts will reach around 10 before year's end. He predicts a double-digit tally for next year too.
The exchange has been re-engaging with companies that delayed IPOs because of market conditions in recent years.
Authorities have also eased listing criteria to attract domestic and foreign companies in new-economy industries such as smart electronics and robotics.
Soravis said part of the reason market activity stalled over the past years is domestic political uncertainty, which weakened investor confidence.
Thailand has changed prime ministers three times between 2023 and 2025, before the current leader, Anutin Charnvirakul, was re-elected through a parliamentary vote in March 2026.
"Things suddenly became predictable and stable... there's a sense of optimism [among investors]," Soravis said.

With a more favorable environment, Thailand has started to attract stronger capital inflows and renewed interest from investors, particularly in new-economy sectors such as semiconductors, Soravis said.
He is expecting companies investing in such industries to potentially list on the SET.
The policy backdrop is encouraging. Thailand recently approved a national semiconductor strategy seeking to attract about $80 billion in investments by 2050.
In the first half of this year, investment applications rose 37% from a year earlier to around 1.47 trillion baht, equivalent to $43.89 billion.
That renewed interest is reflected in trading activity.
Average daily trading volume on the SET, fell over the past three years to around 41 billion baht a day at the end of 2025, before rebounding to about 75 billion baht a day this year, Soravis said.
A recent deal with the New York Stock Exchange could underpin the SET's efforts to energize market activity.
The exchanges signed an agreement this week covering collaboration in areas such as dual listings.
"Our overall objective is to make SET to become a vibrant, dynamic place for issuers to list," Soravis said.
